chapter_title: Sovereignty of the People and Supremacy of this Constitution
chapter_summary: Declares that all sovereign power belongs to the people of Kenya and can only be exercised in accordance with this Constitution. Establishes the Constitution as the supreme law of the Republic.

articles.content: All sovereign power belongs to the people of Kenya and shall be exercised only in accordance with this Constitution.

clauses.content: All sovereign power belongs to the people of Kenya and shall be exercised only in accordance with this Constitution.
The people may exercise their sovereign power either directly or through their democratically elected representatives.

Sovereign power under this Constitution is delegated to Parliament and the legislative assemblies in the county governments, the national executive and executive structures in the county governments, and the Judiciary and independent tribunals.
The sovereign power of the people is exercised at the national level and the county level.

articles.content: This Constitution is the supreme law of the Republic and binds all persons and all State organs at both levels of government.

clauses.content: This Constitution is the supreme law of the Republic and binds all persons and all State organs at both levels of government.
No person may claim or exercise State authority except as authorised under this Constitution.
The validity or legality of this Constitution is not subject to challenge by or before any court or other State organ.
Any law, including customary law, that is inconsistent with this Constitution is void to the extent of the inconsistency, and any act or omission in contravention of this Constitution is invalid.
The general rules of international law shall form part of the law of Kenya.
Any treaty or convention ratified by Kenya shall form part of the law of Kenya under this Constitution.

articles.content: Every person has an obligation to respect, uphold and defend this Constitution.

clauses.content: Every person has an obligation to respect, uphold and defend this Constitution.
Any attempt to establish a government otherwise than in compliance with this Constitution is unlawful.

chapter_summary: Defines Kenya as a multi-party democratic State founded on national values and principles of governance, sets the territory, symbols, languages, national days, and separation of State and religion.

articles.content: Kenya is a sovereign Republic. The Republic of Kenya is a multi-party democratic State founded on the national values and principles of governance referred to in Article 10.

clauses.content: Kenya is a sovereign Republic.
The Republic of Kenya is a multi-party democratic State founded on the national values and principles of governance referred to in Article 10.

articles.content: Kenya consists of the territory and territorial waters comprising Kenya on the effective date, and any additional territory and territorial waters defined by an Act of Parliament.

clauses.content: Kenya consists of the territory and territorial waters comprising Kenya on the effective date, and any additional territory and territorial waters defined by an Act of Parliament.

articles.content: The territory of Kenya is divided into the counties specified in the First Schedule. The governments at the national and county levels are distinct and inter-dependent and shall conduct their mutual relations on the basis of consultation and co-operation.

clauses.content: The territory of Kenya is divided into the counties specified in the First Schedule.
The governments at the national and county levels are distinct and inter-dependent and shall conduct their mutual relations on the basis of consultation and co-operation.
A national State organ shall ensure reasonable access to its services in all parts of the Republic.

articles.content: The national language of the Republic is Kiswahili. The official languages of the Republic are Kiswahili and English. The State shall promote and protect the diversity of language of the people of Kenya.

clauses.content: The national language of the Republic is Kiswahili.
The official languages of the Republic are Kiswahili and English.

The State shall promote and protect the diversity of language of the people of Kenya, and promote the development and use of indigenous languages, Kenyan Sign language, Braille and other communication formats and technologies.

articles.content: There shall be no State religion.

clauses.content: There shall be no State religion.

articles.content: The national symbols of the Republic are the national flag, national anthem, coat of arms, and public seal. The national days are Madaraka Day (1 June), Mashujaa Day (20 October), and Jamhuri Day (12 December).

clauses.content: The national symbols of the Republic are the national flag, the national anthem, the coat of arms, and the public seal.
The national days are Madaraka Day (1st June), Mashujaa Day (20th October), and Jamhuri Day (12th December).

articles.article_title: National values and principles of governance
articles.content: The national values and principles of governance include patriotism, national unity, sharing and devolution of power, the rule of law, democracy and participation of the people; human dignity, equity, social justice, inclusiveness, equality, human rights, non-discrimination and protection of the marginalised; good governance, integrity, transparency and accountability; and sustainable development.

clauses.content: The national values and principles of governance bind all State organs, State officers, public officers and all persons whenever any of them applies or interprets this Constitution, enacts, applies or interprets any law, or makes or implements public policy decisions.

The national values and principles of governance include: patriotism, national unity, sharing and devolution of power, the rule of law, democracy and participation of the people; human dignity, equity, social justice, inclusiveness, equality, human rights, non-discrimination and protection of the marginalised; good governance, integrity, transparency and accountability; and sustainable development.

articles.content: This Constitution recognises culture as the foundation of the nation and as the cumulative civilization of the Kenyan people and nation.

clauses.content: This Constitution recognises culture as the foundation of the nation and as the cumulative civilization of the Kenyan people and nation.

chapter_summary: Covers acquisition, retention, and revocation of Kenyan citizenship by birth or registration, protects dual citizenship, and guarantees passports and identification documents for all citizens.

articles.content: Every citizen is entitled to the rights, privileges and benefits of citizenship, subject to the limits provided or permitted by this Constitution; and a Kenyan passport and any document of registration or identification issued by the State.

clauses.content: Every citizen is entitled to the rights, privileges and benefits of citizenship, subject to the limits provided or permitted by this Constitution; and a Kenyan passport and to any document of registration or identification issued by the State to citizens.

articles.content: Every person who was a citizen immediately before the effective date retains that citizenship. Citizenship may be acquired by birth or registration.

clauses.content: Every person who was a citizen immediately before the effective date retains that citizenship.
Citizenship may be acquired by birth or registration.

articles.content: A person is a citizen by birth if on the day of the person's birth, whether or not the person is born in Kenya, either the mother or the father of the person is a citizen.

clauses.content: A person is a citizen by birth if on the day of the person's birth, whether or not the person is born in Kenya, either the mother or the father of the person is a citizen.

articles.content: A person who has been married to a citizen for a period of at least seven years, or a person who has lawfully resided in Kenya for a continuous period of at least seven years, may apply to be registered as a citizen.

clauses.content: A person who has been married to a citizen for a period of at least seven years may apply to be registered as a citizen.
A person who has lawfully resided in Kenya for a continuous period of at least seven years may apply to be registered as a citizen.

articles.content: A citizen by birth does not lose citizenship by acquiring the citizenship of another country.

clauses.content: A citizen by birth does not lose citizenship by acquiring the citizenship of another country.

articles.content: The Cabinet Secretary may revoke citizenship acquired by registration if obtained by fraud, false representation, concealment of material facts, or disloyalty during war.

clauses.content: Citizenship acquired by registration may be revoked if obtained by fraud, false representation or concealment of any material fact.

articles.content: Parliament shall enact legislation providing for the conditions and procedures for citizenship.

clauses.content: Parliament shall enact legislation providing for the conditions on which citizenship may be acquired and lost.

chapter_summary: Specifies strict procedures for amending the Constitution by parliamentary initiative or popular initiative (referendum requirements for fundamental pillars such as sovereignty, territory, the Bill of Rights, and devolution).
Provides rules of constitutional interpretation, standing to enforce rights (broad locus standi for public interest litigation), and official legal definitions.
Ensures smooth transition from the former Constitution to the 2010 Constitution, outlines consequential legislation timelines, and establishes the effective date (27 August 2010).
